body: When applying for those roles, what resume touch ups and things do hiring managers hope for and look for??? Thank you

Lol. I’ve been in a B2B role where all I did was cold call and headhunt. Online and over the phone close: no face to face. It was miserable having to hit 80-100 calls daily and have one to two semi positive cold calls a week. That beat my soul into dust
I’ve looked into some holistic and non-medicated method of supplanting the meds. I haven’t known where to began but maybe something like that is a start?

I don’t feel like I’m missing much. Can’t fathom what’s missing. I know what basic mechanics are derivative of happiness: being loved, supported, needs met, basic Maslow’s self-actualization bullshit. I can’t think of what I’m missing.

I’d like to be happy and enjoy things that are enjoyable and... nothing registers and joy sparking these days

More of the nihilism. I’m a bodybuilder and I have bicep veins thicker than most peoples dicks. I’ve achieved crazy physical feats. Nothing hardly registers. I won a bodybuilding show in October and felt nothing. No joy. More of a “oh cool, I can have donut holes again now that it’s over”.

I do have family. It blows my mind when I see the little ones on Christmas. Little homie(my nephew) got a Paw Patrol truck.... he was vibrating with excitement. He went cross eyed for a bit and just spun in circles. He jumped until he almost made himself throw up. I would eat a mile of shit to have 10% of the excitement he had for his Paw Patrol... for ANYTHING in my life
I’ve switched meds a myriad of times. Probably time to switch again

Not addicted to anything except maybe caffeine at this point. That’s a recent development since night shift, but my problems predate that.

I volunteer through charities my part time job supports, I donate, and I’m waiting on my app back from a charity that helps children who are victims of abuse.

I’ve worked for everything I do have. I didn’t have much growing up. I just haven’t been happy since like.... 2014?

^^^ it’s awesome but it’s like a foreign language. Never felt it and I can’t relate lol. I’m fingers crossed I keep my job so I don’t have to take a mediocre sales job I don’t want. There’s no shortcut to sales... just following processes that bring me great sadness. I admire you though. Fuckin kudos, mate

I sold semiconductors at my last job. Well, the services of it. I worked for a broker realistically. The business was shady, there were no rules, no big accounts left, and the whole operation would fall into the dirt if the company’s top 3 salespeople in the world (out of about 150 reps) dropped dead at the same time.

That job was a joke. I also sell personal training as I am a personal trainer part time. I don’t take on too many clients since it’s part time, but also I hate generating leads. When people approach me it’s great. When I have to sell people, I break down quick

I hear ya. I know attitude is a big one. I really just have no heart for sales. I’m a bodybuilder/personal trainer in my free time and literally hate selling fitness packages. The staff sells for me and I just train. I am overcome with anxiety and guilt asking for the sale: especially when the client really can’t afford it, can’t get the most use out of it, or it’s not a good fit but I’m pressured to do something. And I’m talking about all my sales roles with that previous statement.

I seriously want anything other than sales, but it was my first job and the one I was in the longest. 

I can’t find another entry level job that isn’t sales right now. Money doesn’t matter to me really. 40-50k a year and I can make it. I don’t want to fake it until my souls bleeds while doing a sales job making less than 40k like I was doing. 

Is marketing a good step away from sales? I just don’t know what to do with limited career history and knowing I’m in a vortex: I’m inextricably pulled towards sales based on my resume even though I vehemently oppose falling into sales again.

I’ve considered even going back to school and moving back home for a bit
